chunks: ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked him about a man who died while there was with him no Muslim man and no Muslim woman from among his relatives, but there were Christian men with him and Muslim women between whom and him there was no kinship. He said:
“The Christian should perform ghusl, then wash him, for necessity has arisen.”

key_terms.اضْطُرَّ: a state of necessity or compulsion
key_terms.قَرَابَةٌ: kinship relation relevant to legal propriety
key_terms.مُسْلِمٌ: a Muslim male eligible in principle to undertake the rite
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he performs ghusl for himself first

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Muslim dies and only Christian men are available to wash the body?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a case of necessity in the washing of the deceased. When no eligible Muslim man or related Muslim woman is available, a Christian man may first perform ghusl and then wash the dead Muslim due to necessity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.436 - Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) about a man who dies and is accompanied by no Muslim men or female Muslim relatives. Instead, there are Christian men and Muslim women unrelated to him.
The Imam said: "The Christian man should first perform ghusl (ritual washing for himself), then wash the deceased, as it is a case of necessity”.
